hits.title: Atypical travel: known egress points
hits.excerpt: The group SASE gateways egress from 203.0.113.0/24 (Amsterdam) and 198.51.100.0/24 (Paris). A sign-in pair inside these ranges within one hour is a gateway hand-over, not travel.

hits.title: Identity Protection triage checklist
hits.excerpt: Confirm MFA outcome, device compliance, and whether the source IP is a corporate egress before escalating.

hits.title: Password spray: playbook
hits.excerpt: Treat the alert as a confirmed password spray when the failed sign-ins in the window reach any of: 100 or more distinct accounts, 5 or more countries, or 25 or more source IPs. Below all three, requalify as noise and tune. On any success from a spray source: reset the password, revoke refresh tokens, and review the account's audit log for authentication methods registered and inbox rules created after the success. Either is follow-on activity; escalate the incident to IR.

hits.title: Legacy authentication: BAV2ROPC
hits.excerpt: The user agent BAV2ROPC is the resource owner password credentials flow used by spray tooling against Exchange Online. It is not subject to interactive MFA where legacy authentication is not blocked; a success through it is a password the attacker now holds.

hits.title: Inbox forwarding rules to external addresses
hits.excerpt: Automatic forwarding to external domains is blocked by transport rule for the whole group, so a client-side inbox rule whose ForwardTo is an external address is the one way mail leaves a mailbox by rule, and a rule filtered on invoice, IBAN, SWIFT or payment terms is business email compromise until shown otherwise. Do: remove the rule, revoke the user's refresh tokens and reset the password, block the destination address at the transport rule, pull the message trace for everything forwarded since the rule was created, and tell the payments desk to hold any change of beneficiary details received in the last 30 days. Escalate to the fraud desk and to IR.

hits.title: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing: replayed sessions
hits.excerpt: A sign-in that satisfies MFA from an address the user has never used, on an unmanaged device, minutes before an inbox rule appears, is the signature of a session token replayed from an adversary-in-the-middle phishing page. MFA satisfied is not evidence that the user signed in. Look for the phishing message and the URL click that preceded the first such sign-in.

hits.title: Configuration management on production Windows servers
hits.excerpt: Production Windows servers are managed by the Contoso configuration agent, cfgagent.exe, installed under C:\Program Files\Contoso\ConfigAgent and running as SYSTEM under the ContosoConfigAgent service. It applies state by launching powershell.exe with -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand, so an encoded command whose parent is cfgagent.exe from that path, as SYSTEM, inside a declared maintenance window, is the expected shape of a run and the agent doing its job. Document the exception on the triplet (device, parent image path, account) in the detection's exclusions for that server; do not disable the rule, since an encoded command from any other parent, from any other path, as any other account, or outside a window is exactly what it exists to catch.

hits.title: LSASS credential access during authorised red team exercises
hits.excerpt: Credential-access techniques against lsass.exe on endpoints are in scope for the purple team exercise PT-2026-0914, whose authorised window is 2026-09-14 01:00 to 06:00 UTC. The operator account svc-purpleops and the source host ws-eng-0148 are on the exercise list. An LSASS read from svc-purpleops on a listed host inside the window is expected and authorised, not an incident; confirm the attack surface reduction block held and that the prevention worked, document the run against the exercise, and do not escalate. An LSASS read from any other account, from any other host, or outside the window is exactly what this rule exists to catch.

hits.title: Identity Protection triage checklist
hits.excerpt: Confirm the outcome, the account priority and whether the activity maps to a change or an authorised exercise before escalating.

hits.title: Kerberoasting alerts from the credentialed vulnerability scanner
hits.excerpt: The credentialed vulnerability scanner svc-vulnscan requests Kerberos service tickets for service principal names across the estate during authenticated scan windows, which fires this rule as apparent Kerberoasting. This is expected and is not Kerberoasting: the scanner obtains the tickets to authenticate to the services it scans, the tickets are AES256 rather than the RC4 downgrade Kerberoasting relies on, and nothing is harvested for offline cracking. Requalify the alert as a false positive and add a tuning exclusion for svc-vulnscan on this rule rather than closing it by hand again; do not escalate. Genuine Kerberoasting shows RC4-downgraded tickets requested by an account that is not the scanner, and tickets that are never followed by authentication to the service.
